// MIT. Additive retained receiving catalog for the one original Datasette provider.
const alias = {type:'string',pattern:'^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$'};
const workspaceId = {type:'string',minLength:1,maxLength:256};
const sha = {type:'string',pattern:'^[a-f0-9]{64}$'};
const path = {type:'string',minLength:1,maxLength:4096};
const exportId = sha;
const selected = {workspace:alias};
const uploadId = {type:'string',pattern:'^[a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[1-8][a-f0-9]{3}-[89ab][a-f0-9]{3}-[a-f0-9]{12}$'};
const decimal = {type:'string',pattern:'^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$',maxLength:10};
const read = {readOnly:true,idempotent:true};
const page = {offset:{type:'integer',minimum:0},limit:{type:'integer',minimum:1,maximum:250}};
const range = {offset:{type:'integer',minimum:0},limit:{type:'integer',minimum:1,maximum:196608},readId:{type:'string',minLength:1,maxLength:64}};

export function datasetteReceivingTools(tool) {
  return [
    tool('merchant_datasette_upload_status',
      'Read the original bounded upload declaration, durable prefix and complete-file result through the existing native file authority. After an interrupted chunk, inspect this same UUID before explicitly continuing.',
      {...selected,uploadId},['workspace','uploadId'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_upload_chunk',
      'Receive one exact original archive range through the native uploadChunk client. Supply canonical decimal byte fields and canonical base64 for at most 8 MiB. Preserve the upload UUID and complete declaration on continuation; the native owner alone retains and publishes the file.',
      {...selected,uploadId,name:{type:'string',minLength:1,maxLength:240},bytes:decimal,sha256:sha,
        offset:decimal,length:decimal,data:{type:'string',maxLength:11184812}},
      ['workspace','uploadId','name','bytes','sha256','offset','length','data'],{readOnly:false,idempotent:true}),
    tool('merchant_datasette_reconnect',
      'Reconnect the original host-declared workspace and verify its persistent identity. Read native status and the actual operation catalog; this does not resume or replay a source, publisher or buyer action.',
      {...selected,workspaceId},['workspace','workspaceId'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_files',
      'Read one complete page of original retained source, edition, publisher, dataset, analysis or export file identities. Follow page.next through the original native catalog.',
      {...selected,prefix:{type:'string',maxLength:4096},...page},['workspace'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_file',
      'Inspect an exact original workspace-relative file and optionally verify its reviewed SHA-256.',
      {...selected,path,sha256:sha},['workspace','path'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_file_read',
      'Receive a bounded chunk of an exact original file through the maintained retained-file reader. The first read acquires the full hash-verified native file; later chunks and reconnects preserve the same SHA.',
      {...selected,path,expectedSha256:sha,...range},['workspace','path','expectedSha256'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_file_release',
      'Release only an existing merchant receiving file handle. The original Datasette workspace and publisher stay with their owner.',
      {...selected,readId:range.readId},['workspace','readId'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_export_prepare',
      'Save a complete receiving manifest from every original retained file matching the optional native prefix. Two complete native inventories must agree. Existing source/workspace archives travel unchanged; this action never generates another native export.',
      {...selected,workspaceId,prefix:{type:'string',maxLength:4096}},['workspace','workspaceId'],{readOnly:false,idempotent:true}),
    tool('merchant_datasette_export_inventory',
      'Read a page from the already-retained complete receiving manifest, including the full original file identities. The complete manifest is always available for download.',
      {...selected,exportId,...page},['workspace','exportId'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_export_manifest',
      'Read the exact byte count and SHA of the complete saved Datasette receiving manifest.',
      {...selected,exportId},['workspace','exportId'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_export_file',
      'Receive a manifest-declared original file using its original export, manifest and file hashes. Preserve offset and readId on continued receiving; after a reader restart use the same original hashes.',
      {...selected,exportId,file:path,expectedManifestSha256:sha,expectedSha256:sha,...range},
      ['workspace','exportId','file','expectedManifestSha256','expectedSha256'],read),
    tool('merchant_datasette_export_file_release',
      'Release this receiving export’s retained file handle without closing its original source owner.',
      {...selected,exportId,readId:range.readId},['workspace','exportId','readId'],read),
  ];
}

# Datasette source editions and complete customer receiving

This is the merchant attachment to the original Datasette workspace. It uses the
same native client, persistent workspace identity, source editions, publisher
history and release packages. The source CLI and industrial browser retain their
existing owner. The merchant attachment exposes that owner’s operations and
receives its complete original files.

## Open the existing workspace

Start the original Datasette CLI with its existing workspace, selected buyer
settings and private launch-file option. Follow the source-owned
`datasette/README.md` for the installed command’s current flags. Its one startup
record uses `stellar-forge.datasette-server.v1` and contains `url`,
`workspaceId` and `instanceId`. Keep the launch file private. The merchant
does not start another Datasette process or acquire another workspace lease.

Declare that launch file in the original connection configuration:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.datasette-workspace-connection.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "geothermal": {
      "label": "Reviewed WRI geothermal source edition",
      "urlFile": "./datasette-launch.json",
      "expectedWorkspaceId": "USE_THE_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_ID",
      "timeoutMs": 300000
    }
  }
}
```

The connection reader resolves `urlFile` relative to this configuration.
Alternatively, declare `urlEnv` with the existing environment variable holding
the native origin. Use exactly one. The server admits its existing loopback
Host/Origin protocol and requires `X-Datasette-Workspace-ID` after health
discovery. The original native client owns those details.

The existing merchant provider is `datasette-workspaces`. Its configuration
input remains `datasetteWorkspaceConnection` and its family remains
`datasetteWorkspaces`. Configure the merchant’s ordinary private
`exportsDirectory` for receiving records. On a shared local machine it must be
outside the native source workspace, so receiving does not insert its own
metadata into the original source inventory. The merchant HTTP listener uses its
existing access token. Tokens and connection URLs belong in host configuration;
a tool caller selects the declared alias.

## Original source and publication operations

Read `merchant_datasette_health`, `merchant_datasette_status` and
`merchant_datasette_operations` before changing an existing workspace.
`merchant_datasette_operation` forwards one complete `operation` and `input`
to the source-owned dispatcher. Its operation enumeration is imported directly
from the source client.

| Native operations | Preserved original behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `source.capture`, `source.adopt`, `source.inspect`, `source.review` | Continue the original source operation, retain complete responses, inspect exact values, and review all source keys and projected types. |
| `editions.create`, `editions.list`, `editions.inspect`, `editions.compare`, `source.select` | Keep immutable edition identity, complete reviewed projection and saved source comparisons. |
| `publisher.status`, `publisher.source`, `publisher.target`, `publisher.plan`, `publisher.extract`, `publisher.inspect`, `publisher.review`, `publisher.publish`, `publisher.recover` | Use the existing typed dataset publisher, candidate/run history, exact review and target revision. |
| `publisher.buyer-offer`, `publisher.prepare-buyer`, `release.prepare`, `release.stage` | Keep the original published snapshot, buyer terms and complete source/release package. |
| `source.export`, `source.receive`, `workspace.export`, `workspace.receive` | Export and receive the original source-edition or full editable-workspace archive using its maintained archive engine. |
| `files.list`, `files.inspect`, `files.read` | Read complete original file identities and exact native byte ranges. |
| `operations.inspect`, `operations.cancel` | Inspect a saved capture/extraction by its original ID or cancel the actual active native operation. |

The source client declares the original 31 native operations and, in the joined
request-recovery edition, `requests.inspect` and `requests.list`. The merchant
tool catalog has five original control tools plus twelve upload and receiving
tools. Catalog presence is
separate from an operation being executed; receiving reports record the actual
calls and files.

Keep a capture’s `operationId`, an extraction’s `runId`, and the original
edition/review/target identities. No transport retries a mutating native action
automatically. A timeout or lost response leaves its outcome uncertain. Read
native status and `operations.inspect` with the same saved identity before
using the source’s documented continuation or publisher recovery. Reconnect does
not issue the interrupted action.

For example, inspecting an already-retained edition requires its existing ID:

```json
{
  "workspace": "geothermal",
  "operation": "editions.inspect",
  "input": {"id": "THE_SAVED_EDITION_ID", "offset": 0, "limit": 250}
}
```

## Upload a complete reviewed archive

Use the original upload UUID, original filename, exact decimal byte count and
whole-file SHA-256. The same native file authority retains the declaration,
durable prefix and original chunk history. Its existing workspace gate owns
cancellation and shutdown; the merchant attaches that owner.

`merchant_datasette_upload_status` reads the original declaration and
`merchant_datasette_upload_chunk` forwards one original range through the
native client. Tool byte fields remain decimal strings. Its `data` is canonical
base64 for at most 8 MiB; the native request body is the exact decoded bytes.
The selected provider declares a 12 MiB MCP request ceiling for that encoding.
The original native operation JSON ceiling remains 1 MiB.

The SDK and CLI transfer a complete reviewed local file with bounded buffers:

~~~sh
starforge datasette-mcp upload \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8123/mcp \
  --workspace geothermal \
  --upload-id ORIGINAL_UPLOAD_UUID \
  --file /private/customer/wri-geothermal.sfds.gz \
  --name wri-geothermal.sfds.gz \
  --bytes 59792 \
  --sha256 53f2486406d61f18c9e1c9ceaac659c265bbad7afe2fe54b1a17f43307cb0ca0
~~~

Those bytes identify the original retained WRI source archive; a different
archive must use its own reviewed declaration. Before the first chunk the
helper hashes the complete private regular file and verifies its original size.
An existing upload must match all four declaration fields, and its durable
prefix must match those same local bytes. The helper then sends complete ranges
of 1 MiB by default, or the selected 64 KiB–8 MiB size. It keeps one native UUID
and does not create a separate upload ledger or workspace.

A failed chunk stops without automatic repetition. Read its actual state with:

~~~sh
starforge datasette-mcp upload-status \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8123/mcp \
  --workspace geothermal \
  --upload-id ORIGINAL_UPLOAD_UUID
~~~

Explicitly run the same upload command to continue. The original authority
verifies the committed prefix before discarding only an uncheckpointed partial
suffix. FINALIZABLE permits the native zero-byte finish at the complete length.
COMPLETE returns its original archiveFile and retainedFile. REJECTED retains the
original failure and bytes; correcting a declaration requires another reviewed
UUID. Local file changes stop the transfer without replacing native history.

After COMPLETE, explicitly pass that native archiveFile and SHA to the existing
source.receive operation with a stable destination id, or to workspace.receive
with the selected receiving directory. Those unchanged engines validate and
receive the archive. An upload alone does not capture, approve, publish or restore
a dataset.

The SDK equivalent is `client.uploadFile({path,uploadId,name,bytes,sha256})`.
Its result retains state, the complete native upload reply, the reviewed local
identity and resumedBytes. The standalone `uploadDatasetteFile` function
accepts the same fields with the original merchant URL/alias or client.

## Preserve the source’s meaning

Source rows expose `cellTypes` alongside exact source text. A numeric lexeme,
a string containing digits and a null value remain distinct. Do not pass source
numbers through JavaScript `Number` merely to display or export them.

The original retained WRI geothermal input contains four pages with 50, 50, 50
and 39 rows. Those page bodies omit the columns array: use the ordered columns
from their original table metadata and manifest. The observed source key
`gppd_idnr` was unique and nonblank across those 189 rows; the database metadata
declares no primary key. `rowid` is the source locator. In the original schema
`commissioning_year` is REAL and has fractional values; `wepp_id` is TEXT and
can contain compound values. Preserve original nulls and sparse year coverage.

Keep advertised, requested and final page URLs separately. The retained capture
records an HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrade. Preserve unavailable HTTP status/headers for
the two originally received Notion pages as unavailable. The merchant does not
recapture those pages or manufacture missing transport receipts.

The distinct `datasette-analysis/` customer application consumes the original
source edition or prepared/finalized DatasetDelivery through its existing
AnalysisWorkspace. This attachment receives that application’s files when they
are retained in the source workspace, and receives its complete archive when the
owner includes it in the native delivery. It does not create a second Analysis
store or silently copy an unrelated outside directory into the source.

## Prepare complete receiving

First complete the intended native source/publisher/customer operations. If the
customer needs an editable workspace, call the original `workspace.export`
once through its existing owner and retain its returned archive identity. A
source edition alone uses `source.export`. Both return `retainedFile` when
the export is inside the original workspace. The maintained native
`workspace.receive` or `source.receive` later consumes that exact archive
and its SHA-256.

Then call:

```json
{
  "workspace": "geothermal",
  "workspaceId": "THE_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_ID"
}
```

with `merchant_datasette_export_prepare`. An optional `prefix` restricts the
selection to an original relative prefix such as `exports/` or `captures/`.
Omitting it includes the complete original retained-file inventory. No source
export is generated by this receiving action.

The adapter receives every inventory page, requires the terminal native cursor,
and compares a second complete inventory. If files change between these reads,
preparation fails explicitly. The resulting content-addressed `exportId`
binds every path, byte count and SHA. Repeating preparation for identical native
inventory produces the same export and verifies the same saved record.

The saved package contains:

* `Datasette-Download.json`: the complete receiving manifest and persistent
  workspace identity.
* `native-manifest.json`: a deterministic receiving record containing all
  original `files.list` responses, their pagination and complete descriptors.
  This is generated from returned native identities; it is not represented as a
  raw provider HTTP response.
* `files/<original-relative-path>`: each original native file with unchanged
  bytes, including source responses, reviews, edition history, publisher and
  dataset output, and the existing portable archives selected by the inventory.

The native inventory currently supports 30,000 files of up to 2 GiB each.
Manifest limits are 64 MiB. Original file byte counts arrive as explicit decimal
strings; the receiver verifies their safe integer range for filesystem access.
There is no preview-row or shortened-file substitution. Unsupported names or
limits cause an explicit error rather than dropping a member.

## Download, resume and reopen

`merchant_datasette_export_inventory` pages the saved manifest for inspection.
`merchant_datasette_export_manifest` returns its complete byte identity.
`merchant_datasette_export_file` uses the existing retained reader; it accepts
the original export, manifest SHA, file SHA, offset and optional `readId`.
The corresponding release tool closes only that receiving file handle.

The first read streams the complete selected native file through
`files.read`, verifies all original ranges and the whole SHA, and transfers a
private read-only descriptor to the maintained RetainedFileReads engine.
Memory stays bounded while large original files are received. Subsequent chunks
come from that verified descriptor. The original native file can later change
without changing this already-received snapshot. A new reader must still obtain
the originally requested bytes and SHA or fail explicitly.

The customer client uses the original RetainedDownload engine for complete-file
publication, existing partial ranges, exact completion manifests and its normal
Linux `flock` receiving lease. After a reader restart, the same original
manifest/file SHA and offset reopen the same bytes. Completed customer files stay
in the original receiving directory. A different native version never replaces
them silently.

```sh
starforge datasette-mcp download \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8123/mcp \
  --workspace geothermal \
  --export ORIGINAL_EXPORT_ID \
  --directory /private/customer/geothermal \
  --manifest-sha256 ORIGINAL_MANIFEST_SHA256
```

The access token is read from the original `MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment
variable, or from the explicitly selected `--token-env`. Keep its value private.

Run offline verification after the merchant and native listeners close:

```sh
starforge datasette-mcp reopen \
  --export ORIGINAL_EXPORT_ID \
  --directory /private/customer/geothermal \
  --manifest-sha256 ORIGINAL_MANIFEST_SHA256
```

This reopens the original receiving lease and verifies every complete local
member against the saved full manifest. It performs no source request, native
publication, buyer action or archive restore. Use the original archive receiving
command separately when opening the editable workspace.

## JavaScript client

```js
import {
  openDatasetteClient,
  reopenDatasetteExport
} from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/operator/datasette';

const client = await openDatasetteClient({
  url: merchantUrl,
  tokenEnv: 'MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN',
  workspace: 'geothermal'
});

const health = await client.health();
const prepared = await client.exportPrepare({
  workspaceId: health.native.workspaceId
});
const received = await client.downloadExport({
  exportId: prepared.exportId,
  expectedManifestSha256: prepared.manifestFile.sha256,
  directory: receivingDirectory
});

const reopened = await reopenDatasetteExport({
  directory: receivingDirectory,
  exportId: received.exportId,
  expectedManifestSha256: prepared.manifestFile.sha256
});
```

A configured client alias cannot be overridden by a later call or download.
The complete original native actions are also exposed as named methods, such as
`sourceInspect({input:{operationId,offset:0,limit:250}})`,
`publisherInspect({input:{runId}})` and
`workspaceExport({input:{outputFile}})`. These forward the unchanged native
input and do not add a replay policy.

## Receiving exercise and ownership

The companion receiving program attaches the existing merchant HTTP tool
handler to the exact source-owned provider, reads its actual advertised names,
inspects the retained source edition, receives all declared native files, closes
and reattaches the merchant component, then verifies complete offline receiving.
When its owner supplies originalUpload, it also inspects and zero-byte replays
that exact completed upload, verifying the unchanged native reply and retained
file. Its report includes actual native workspace/edition/export IDs, advertised
and invoked tool names, upload outcome, calls and file hashes. It does not launch another Python or Node source owner, capture provider
pages, create a new review, dispatch a buyer payment or repeat publication.

The merchant attachment drains its own in-flight callbacks and retained file
handles on close. The original native workspace, publisher and browser remain
with their original owner. Complete native source, publisher and customer
operation results remain separate from this attachment’s receiving report.

### Original source references

* Datasette source/workspace contract and retained-file implementation:
  source owner’s PR 2281 and complete source packet
  `dab756bbcb31fe55da4bfd2265b7e525e8d80f39` in
  `woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026`.
* Original WRI retained seven-file source:
  `57fda4e96952ca5c2a28d738f87ba2c774aee194` in the same repository.
* Customer Analysis contribution: PR 2287,
  `12d9a9280d2159ebbfd3a2d45b19de7eb07e9797`.
* Source provider’s `client.mjs`, `workspace.mjs`, `provider.mjs`,
  `editions.mjs` and `archive.mjs` remain authoritative for the installed
  native catalog and exact input shapes.

# Datasette: complete merchant receiving on the original workspace

This program receives a finished Datasette workspace through the same source-owned merchant provider. It does not open the source, publisher, seller, payer or Analysis workspace. The original native server stays open and retains its own lease.

The native source owner should finish source capture, edition review, publisher/customer work and its ordinary full workspace export before running this attachment. Keep the original workspace idle during the receiving snapshot. The receiver writes its own private MCP configuration, file inventory, download and operating journal. When given the original completed upload declaration, it also submits that same native upload's zero-byte replay; no new file bytes, source action or upload identity are created.

## Existing source and input

Use a complete repository-shaped installed source directory containing both stellar/ and stellar-forge/. Its Datasette provider must contain the 17-tool upload/receiving composition and the original 31 native operations, with the two original request-history operations when that source join is present. The source-owned provider has privateExports: true, uses the original provider concurrency policy and loads the maintained Datasette receiving leaf. No npm dependency or MCP SDK is required by this receiving program; Node builtins and the original Linux flock helper are sufficient.

The source owner supplies:

- Its existing private Datasette launch JSON or URL file, already used by its browser/CLI.
- The persistent original workspace ID.
- The reviewed edition ID and exact edition JSON SHA-256.
- The original capture operation ID and, when available, exact capture JSON SHA-256.
- The expected complete source row count.
- The relative path, exact byte count and SHA-256 of its already-exported original workspace archive.
- The optional exact completed source upload declaration `{uploadId,name,bytes,sha256}`. Supply it for the original raw-upload customer journey; all four values come from the existing native upload receipt.
- Any additional expected native files, such as the source edition archive or a customer/publisher handoff, that must be present in this complete receiving.

The program verifies the edition and capture through every original native page. It preserves the original ordered columns, cell values and explicit cell types; it does not convert exact number tokens through JavaScript arithmetic. The WRI geothermal operation uses 189 rows and 26 ordered columns. Its original metadata supplies the column order because the captured pages omit columns. The observed unique gppd_idnr values remain a reviewed key rather than an invented database primary key.

## One callable attachment

Import runDatasetteMcpReceiving from this directory's run-receiving.mjs and call it inside the same invocation that already owns the native workspace:

~~~js
await runDatasetteMcpReceiving({
  sourceRoot: absoluteInstalledSource,
  connectionFile: originalPrivateLaunchFile,
  outputDirectory: distinctPrivateReceivingDirectory,
  workspaceAlias: 'portfolio',
  expectedWorkspaceId: originalState.workspaceId,
  editionId: reviewedEdition.id,
  expectedEditionSha256: reviewedEdition.editionSha256,
  captureId: originalCapture.operationId,
  expectedCaptureSha256: originalCapture.captureSha256,
  expectedRows: 189,
  workspaceArchive: {
    path: originalArchive.retainedFile.path,
    bytes: originalArchive.retainedFile.bytes,
    sha256: originalArchive.retainedFile.sha256
  },
  requiredNativeFiles: [],
  originalUpload: {
    uploadId: originalUploadedSource.uploadId,
    name: originalUploadedSource.name,
    bytes: originalUploadedSource.bytes,
    sha256: originalUploadedSource.sha256
  }
});
~~~

These values come from the original native results. A receiving directory must be distinct from the original native workspace and must either be empty or contain this same program's saved journey. Do not select the native owner's journal directory.

For command-line use, save those exact fields as a private JSON input and run:

~~~sh
node operations/scf-datasette-mcp-receiving-20261012/run-receiving.mjs --input /absolute/private/receiving-input.json
~~~

The program does not start or stop the native Datasette server. On completion the original owner can continue its ordinary shutdown, publisher or independent archive restore procedure. The receiving program closes its own two successive merchant listeners, original provider attachments, retained file readers and output lease.

## What is operated

The receiver validates the actual HTTP tool catalog, not just a count from source. It verifies all 17 advertised merchant tool names. With originalUpload it invokes all 17, including status and the exact completed upload's zero-byte replay. A source captured without an upload uses the 15 applicable tools and records that distinction. The report separately records the original 31 or 33 native operation names; catalog presence is not a claim that every native action ran. Source/edition/operation inspection and original file reads do not repeat publication or payment.

The operating sequence is:

1. Attach the host-declared original workspace, verify persistent identity and idle state, then retain the complete source/native operation catalog. If originalUpload is supplied, read its COMPLETE status, zero-byte replay that same upload, and require the unchanged original outcome.
2. Page through every original capture and reviewed edition row, preserving ordered columns, numeric lexemes, nulls and cell types, and verify their complete equality.
3. Read every page of the original retained-file catalog and verify the required edition, capture, full workspace archive and any additional declared publisher/customer files.
4. Open and release a real native retained file handle, then prepare a content-addressed receiving manifest after two complete original inventories agree.
5. Receive every manifest-declared file through the existing chunk reader and original durable downloader. No native export is recreated.
6. Close only the merchant attachment. Reopen the same merchant endpoint and original workspace, select the exact saved manifest, and resume the complete download in its original directory.
7. Re-read original file and workspace identities, close the second merchant attachment, and verify every local received file through the original offline reopen engine.

The downloaded directory contains Datasette-Download.json, the generated complete native-manifest.json and all original retained bytes under files/. The generated native inventory is labeled as a representation of native file-list results; original capture/request/response bytes travel separately and unchanged.

The original workspace archive is one of those exact native files. It remains the artifact for the owner's normal editable restore. A merchant receiving manifest is not substituted for that original archive.

## Durable outputs

journey.json retains the exact input binding, original source/status identities, receiving export and manifest hashes, all tool invocations with input and returned-result hashes, listener close results, errors and complete outcome.

observed/ contains the complete actual tool catalog, native operation catalog, capture and edition pages, original operation record, full native and receiving file inventories, original and resumed download results, native state before and after, and offline full-file verification.

received/ contains every manifest-declared original file and the existing durable download checkpoints. merchant-exports/ contains only the original provider's private receiving records.

Preserve the entire receiving directory with the source owner's final customer package before an ephemeral host exits. The program does not claim external artifact custody.

## Interrupted receiving

Run the same input against the same directory. The original config hash, source state, file inventory, capture, edition, archive and receiving manifest must still match. Read-only native calls can be reissued. A supplied originalUpload permits only its same COMPLETE zero-byte replay; no new source, review, publisher, buyer or upload-body mutation is issued.

An original native state/file change produces an explicit stop. Inspect the native owner and the saved journey before deciding whether a new, separately reviewed receiving snapshot is needed. An occupied old merchant port is also explicit: the program will not silently change the endpoint bound to an existing download checkpoint.

A stopped chunk reader is process-local. The original downloader resumes its verified local byte prefix using the same export, manifest and file SHA. Already completed files are rehashed and reused.

When journey.json is already COMPLETE, rerunning the program verifies all recorded evidence and the received files locally. It does not open either listener. The original complete result stays intact.

## Source ownership

The source/capture/edition/publisher/archive engines and native HTTP owner remain the original Datasette contribution. The additional code lives in stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/ and this receiving directory. The one original provider imports its pure catalog and lazily loads the receiving leaf. Its existing withWorkspace connection latch, cancellation concurrency and close/drain stay authoritative.

The customer Analysis workflow remains in datasette-analysis/. If the operator wants those customer artifacts in this same merchant receiving, its original source owner must first retain them within the complete native file inventory or identify the separate complete Analysis package. This receiver never invents external files or truncates an unavailable customer artifact into a link.

# Receiving an original Datasette archive

The original Datasette retained-file authority accepts a complete source-edition archive or whole-workspace archive in bounded byte ranges. It retains the caller's upload UUID, original filename, byte count and SHA-256 before the first body byte. The completed file is then an input to the existing `source.receive` or `workspace.receive` operation.

This is a file intake step. Source review, edition creation, the publisher, dataset versions, customer Analysis and the original archive receivers continue through their existing operations.

## Original owner and methods

`retainedDatasetteFiles({directory, workspaceId})` preserves its existing `inspect`, `list`, `read` and `relativeName` methods. It also supplies:

```js
await files.uploadStatus({ uploadId });
await files.receiveUpload(
  { uploadId, name, bytes, sha256, offset, length },
  originalRawByteStream,
  { signal: originalOperationAbortController.signal }
);
await files.close();
```

The caller must be the current Datasette workspace owner. Put each `receiveUpload` call inside that workspace's existing active-operation gate, using the original upload UUID as its operation identity. Its controller owns cancellation. Abort and drain the current stream, close this file authority, and then release the original workspace lease. The helper opens no lease and launches no background process.

The helper serializes its file-intake work and status reads. That queue does not replace the workspace's gate against concurrent capture, edition, archive or publisher writes. Keep the original source and publisher dispatch records and their existing request-recovery semantics.

## Declared input

| Field | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| `uploadId` | One caller-retained lowercase UUID. Keep it across interruptions and exact repeated ranges. |
| `name` | The original file basename, at most 240 UTF-8 bytes, without path separators or control characters. |
| `bytes` | Complete original file size as canonical decimal text. The limit is 2 GiB. |
| `sha256` | Lowercase SHA-256 of all original file bytes. |
| `offset` | Start of this raw range as canonical decimal text. |
| `length` | Exact raw request body length as canonical decimal text, at most 8 MiB. |

Use strings such as `"59792"` and `"0"`; numeric JSON values are rejected. The byte range must fit the complete declared size. At most 32,768 nonempty range checkpoints are retained. Each checkpoint records its exact offset, length and chunk SHA-256, so smaller ranges can be repeated after a response is lost without rewriting them.

The same upload UUID cannot be rebound to another name, total size or SHA-256. A repeated range must have the same offset, length and byte hash as one of its recorded chunks. An arbitrary overlap or a differently partitioned earlier prefix is rejected.

The server wrapper keeps its original authentication, Origin, loopback/workspace-identity checks and request admission. Forward the raw byte stream to this method; do not buffer or embed a large archive in the normal 1 MiB operation envelope. Bound the declared raw request by the helper's chunk limit. If the method rejects before consuming a request body, preserve its complete JSON error while safely ending or draining that request through the existing server transport.

## State and interruption recovery

`uploadStatus` is a read. It verifies the durable prefix and returns the original declaration, received byte count, prefix SHA-256, chunk count and maximum chunk size. The immutable source filename and total SHA-256 remain visible on every returned state.

| State | Meaning and continuation |
| --- | --- |
| `RECEIVING` | The saved `receivedBytes` prefix is durable and hash verified. Continue at that exact offset. |
| `FINALIZABLE` | All declared bytes and the full SHA agree, but the completed publication/receipt is unfinished. An empty range at the total byte offset finishes that same upload. |
| `COMPLETE` | The original private file and final hash are verified. The result supplies `archiveFile` and its native `retainedFile` descriptor. |
| `REJECTED` | All received bytes are retained but their full SHA differs from the original declaration. The error includes the actual hash. No archive path is released for receiving. |

After an interrupted raw request, read the original status before continuing. A recorded `uncheckpointedBytes` suffix is not part of the durable prefix. On the next admitted continuation, the helper verifies the saved prefix before truncating only its own unfinished partial suffix and writing the requested range.

A fresh process rehashes the saved prefix with a 256 KiB buffer. Within one process, a small incremental-hash cache is reused only when the private inode, length, times, mode and link count still match. Range bodies and complete files are never loaded into memory as a whole.

A completed publication whose response was lost stays the same upload. An exact earlier chunk returns the verified current result with `replayed: true`; an empty range at the complete byte offset also returns that result. The helper never changes source or edition selections during either path.

If the original upload ID has no saved declaration, `DATASETTE_UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND` is returned with HTTP status 404. Re-read the current native workspace identity and original request before deciding whether that same request can start. Missing declarations beside existing payload files, different declarations, changed prefixes, unexpected links and unrelated destinations are rejected explicitly.

## Retained files and publication

The original workspace owns:

```text
imports/uploads/<uploadId>/upload.json
imports/uploads/<uploadId>/payload.part
imports/uploads/<uploadId>/file/<original-name>
```

The partial path exists only while receiving or completing publication. The metadata preserves every committed chunk and its source declaration. Final publication creates the destination without replacing any other file, syncs it, removes only the same staged inode and verifies the completed file through the original `files.inspect` method before saving `COMPLETE`.

An interrupted publication that left both names is resumed only when both names are the same exact inode and the saved complete byte count/SHA agree. The normal file authority continues to require one private regular-file link after publication.

Both the completed original file and its upload history are visible through the existing file inventory and complete workspace export. The current original exclusion of `dataset/control.json` and `dataset/control.sock` is preserved; dataset versions and snapshots remain retained.

## Applying a completed archive

Use the returned values directly:

```js
const upload = await files.uploadStatus({ uploadId });
if (upload.state !== 'COMPLETE') {
  throw new Error('Finish the original upload before receiving its archive.');
}

await workspace.dispatch('source.receive', {
  archiveFile: upload.archiveFile,
  sha256: upload.sha256,
  id: retainedEditionReceivingId
});
```

For a complete workspace, pass the same `archiveFile` and `sha256` to the existing `workspace.receive` with an explicitly selected receiving directory. That original receiver owns archive validation, source/edition/publisher/customer history, no-overwrite checks and cold reopen.

The browser should retain the original upload ID, declaration and last confirmed range in its existing pending-operation record. Display progress, the original filename and the actionable state. Keep full hashes and checkpoint history available in details. A successful file intake becomes reviewable source input; it does not itself approve an edition or publish a merchant dataset.
